catalog_quote: El acento en la lengua kickapoo se presenta en la antepenúltima sílaba de la palabra. ... Hay pocos casos en los que se registra fonéticamente el acento en la penúltima sílaba, pero en ellos el núcleo silábico está constituido siempre por una vocal larga. Esto permite, desde el punto de vista fonológico, considerar que la vocal larga corresponde en realidad a la expresión de dos vocales cortas idénticas pertenecientes a dos sílabas fonológicas distintas. El acento, entonces, recae en la primera de ellas. [p. 58] ... Cuando fonéticamente aparece una secuencia de dos vocales idénticas, la posición del acento va a determinar si se considera vocal larga, o bien dos vocales. Si el acento va en la penúltima sílaba, se considera que son dos vocales iguales, representando dos moras, la primera de ellas acentuada ... Si el acento aparece en la antepenúltima sílaba, la vocal será considerada larga. [p. 71] ... Un rasgo prosódico –que no tiene función distintiva, sino delimitativa– es el acento, ya que su aparición se considera regular. El acento ocurre en la antepenúltima sílaba, aunque existen casos en los que se presenta en la penúltima. Este hecho coincide siempre con la aparición de vocal larga ... [pp. 93-94] ... Otro signo demarcativo afonemático positivo es el acento, el cual se encuentra fijo en la antepenúltima sílaba de la palabra [p. 95]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: El acento en la lengua kickapoo se presenta en la antepenúltima sílaba de la palabra. [p. 58] ... Un rasgo prosódico –que no tiene función distintiva, sino delimitativa– es el acento, ya que su aparición se considera regular. El acento ocurre en la antepenúltima sílaba, aunque existen casos en los que se presenta en la penúltima. Este hecho coincide siempre con la aparición de vocal larga por lo que se ha preferido describirlo fonológicamente de manera siguiente: cuando el núcleo silábico está formado por una vocal larga y ésta va acentuada, se divide en dos vocales cortas, que corresponden a dos moras, en donde el acento recae en la primera de ellas. [pp. 93-94]
new_statements.translation: Accent in the Kickapoo language falls on the antepenultimate syllable of the word. [p. 58] ... A prosodic feature which has no distinctive function but a delimitative one is the accent, since its occurrence is considered regular. The accent occurs on the antepenultimate syllable, although there are cases in which it appears on the penult. This always coincides with the presence of a long vowel, so it has been preferred to describe it phonologically as follows: when the syllable nucleus consists of a long vowel and that vowel is accented, it is split into two short vowels corresponding to two moras, with the accent falling on the first of them. [pp. 93-94]

El acento, entonces, recae en la primera de ellas" ([a'naa.kwa] 'estrella'); "la única excepción a la regla del acento automát…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary accent is automatic (non-phonemic, demarcative) on the antepenultimate syllable of the word; when the phonetic accent lands on a penultimate long vowel, the long vowel is counted as two moras with accent on the first, so the rule is in effect 'third mora/vowel from the end' (Moctezuma's mora count; the same as Voorhis 1974 p. 14 'third accentable vowel from the end', as reported by Moctezuma p. 107). Kickapoo has phonemic vowel length; Voorhis 1982 (pp. 82-84) additionally treats level vs. falling pitch on long vowels as tied to a sentence accent that reaches only the last three syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Moctezuma p. 59: imperatives carry a secondary accent on the final syllable after the primary accent (e.g. ['pîa.nú] 'come', [ne'paa.nú] 'go to sleep'). No rhythmic secondary stress described.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent on the fourth syllable from the end in the tens numerals (20, 30, 40..), where the accent shifts to the last syllable of the numeral root before the never-accented three-syllable enclitic -pitaki (e.g. nisuá:pitaki 'twenty'); some unpossessed body-part nouns show the same fourth-from-end accent in free variation with regular antepenultimate accent ([uh'ta.ka.ma.I] ~ [uh.ta'ka.ma.I] 'ear'); frequency described as very low. Contradiction with Voorhis: Moctezuma p. 99 reports that Voorhis 1974 p. 8 gives the minimal pair poohkamáaki 'peaches' vs poohkámaaki 'in a peach' from which accent is inferred to be phonemic; Voorhis 1982 pp. 82-84 (opened) treats the difference as level vs. falling pitch on long vowels realized under a sentence accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, phonetic transcriptions of citation forms elicited from Kickapoo speakers of El Nacimiento, Múzquiz, Coahuila (fieldwork 1980-83, 1988, 2010). Moctezuma treats the accent as non-phonemic ('fonético') and delimitative. Voorhis 1982 frames accent as a sentence-level phenomenon.
new_statements.identity_note: Moctezuma Zamarrón 2011 describes the Mexican Kickapoo of El Nacimiento (Múzquiz, Coahuila) — the same language kick1244 (no separate Glottolog dialect code seen); Voorhis's work (1967/1974/1982) describes the US (Oklahoma/Kansas) Kickapoo. Moctezuma (pp. 99, 107) reports Voorhis's rule for the US variety as equivalent ('third accentable vowel from the end'), but Voorhis 1982 treats accent as sentence-level with pitch contrasts, and Gathercole 1983 calls the pitch system tonal, so the catalog entry should note the pitch/tone dimension.

sources.citation: Voorhis, Paul. 1982. The Kickapoo Sound System and Kickapoo Standard Orthography. In William Cowan (ed.), Papers of the Thirteenth Algonquian Conference, 81-89. Ottawa: Carleton University.
sources.note: Pp. 82-84: long vowels contrast level vs. falling pitch (from old vowel clusters); falling pitch is only 'potential', realized when it coincides with the 'sentence accent'; before the sentence accent the contrast merges; the merger is complete in 'that part of a word which is beyond reach of sentence accent, namely, earlier than the third syllable from the last'. No explicit word-stress rule; accent treated at sentence level, marked by pitch diacritics (acute = level, circumflex = falling).
